newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Big buyer boosts Belgian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Big buyer boosts Belgian bonds.

text.p: One large domestic buyer filling a portfolio boosted the Belgian linear bond market on Wednesday for the second successive day, attracting in other buyers, with more rises expected, traders said.

"It is the same buyer as yesterday. He spent about 20 billion francs yesterday and another 10 to 15 billion today," one trader said. "In another couple of days we expect him to start selling the long end."
Traders noted activity centred on five to seven year maturity paper as the lone buyer lured other players into the market, although light selling emerged towards the close.
"This market has not much liquidity, so it reacts strongly to buying or selling pressure," one trader said.
At one stage on Wednesday the spread between the benchmark Belgian 2006 OLO and German Bunds narrowed to a record low of 15 basis points before selling emerged to push it back out again.
But traders said the focus on the 10-year bond was misguided, noting that the spread on five-year paper was just three basis points and on seven-years it was flat.
"Most of the two to eight-years are trading flat against Germany. By comparison the 10-year is very expensive," one trader said.
The 2006 OLO ended the day yielding 6.26 percent against Tuesday's closing 6.34, and the spread over Bunds was 17 basis points against 18.
The front month futures contract was 35 basis points higher at 119.17, having traded in a 119.24/118.99 range.
